sentences.text: By the impugned award, the learned tribunal has awarded Rs.13,24,839/- as compensation to the appellants/claimants with 7.5% interest per annum on account of death of deceased Manish Kumar Verma @ Rahul Verma in an unfortunate accident which took place on 05.02.2015 when the deceased was coming back to his home on a motorcycle, and when he reached at Panikar Dhaba, at that time, the respondent No. 1 drove the vehicle Metador bearing Registration No. C.G.- 10K-1114 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed his bike on the back side and on account of which he sustained multiple injuries and consequently died.

2) As per the pleadings of the claim application filed under Section 166 of the MV Act, the deceased was working as Unit Attendant in Dainik Bhaskar Press Bilaspur and used to earn Rs.12,000/- per month.
The appellants/claimants being parents, Siblings and grandparents of the deceased had filed the claim application claiming total compensation of Rs.51,63,000/-.
3) The claim application was resisted by respondents/driver, owner and insurance company of the offending vehicle on various grounds.
4) The learned tribunal on the basis of pleadings of the parties framed issues and after appreciation of evidence and material available on record awarded the compensation as stated above.
5) Learned counsel for appellants/claimants submits that the impugned award by the claims Tribunal is bad in law, perverse, thus liable to be modified and enhanced.
He further submits that the learned claims Tribunal has failed to apply a multiplier 17 instead of 18.

Apart from this, learned counsel for appellants has Neutral Citation also submitted that there were two dependents on the deceased namely his father and mother, therefore deduction for personal expenses should be 1/3,
whereas the tribunal has assessed only one dependent upon the deceased.
The compensation awarded on other heads is also on the lower side.
6) Learned counsel for respondents No. 1 & 2 filed their joint written statement, in which they denied the contents of the petition.
They have stated that accident has taken place due to negligence of deceased himself as he collided with the other vehicle.
The vehicle with which the deceased met with an accident had fled from the spot and their vehicle was involved in the case.
They have further stated that the vehicle was insured with respondent No. 3 so he is not liable to pay any compensation.
7) Learned counsel for respondent No.3 supported the award and submits that the compensation has rightly been awarded and does not require any interference by this Court.
He has filed his written statement in which he denied the contents of the petition and stated that deceased was not earning Rs. 12000/- per month.

The respondent No. 1 was not having a valid and effective driving license even though the respondent No. 2 appointed him for driving the vehicle, they have violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, therefore, they are not liable to pay any amount of compensation.

Neutral Citation this finding is hereby maintained.

For the forgoing reasons, the appeal is allowed in part.
The amount of compensation of Rs.13,24,839/- awarded by the tribunal is enhanced to Rs.15,01,006/-.

Hence, after deducting the amount of Rs.13,24,839/-, the claimants are held entitled for an additional amount of Rs.1,76,167/-,
the additional amount shall carry interest @6% per annum from the date of claim application.
The insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced amount of compensation within 60 days.
11) The impugned award stands modified to the above extent.
On deposit tribunal shall pass appropriate order with regard to Neutral Citation apportionment, investment and disbursement of the enhance amount of compensation.
12) Appeal thus partly allowed.
